hyperedges.label: Hexagonal Auth Flow: Controller → UseCase Port → Service Implementation
Auth Result DTO Chain: AuthResult → AuthResponse (API boundary mapping)
User Domain Entity with JPA Persistable Pattern and Role Conversion
JWT Security Filter Chain: SecurityConfig registers JwtAuthFilter which delegates token validation to JwtService
Webhook Payment Flow: HandleWebhookService processes payment events, updates Subscription state, and publishes PaymentConfirmedEvent
BillingController orchestrates three billing use cases: checkout creation, webhook handling, and subscription retrieval
Payment Gateway Adapter Pattern — all three adapters implement PaymentGatewayPort for multi-gateway payment support
Subscription Expiry Flow — job loads ACTIVE subscriptions, calls expire(), saves, publishes SubscriptionExpiredEvent
Catalog Product Write Flow — ProductController delegates to use cases, services load/mutate/save Product domain entity
Stock Lifecycle: reserve → sell/release via Order events
hyperedges.rationale: All three nodes participate in the stock state machine: ReserveStockService reserves stock ahead of payment, StockEventListener confirms (sell) or cancels (release) the reservation based on Order module events, and Stock holds the state.

hyperedges.label: Catalog Hexagonal Architecture: UseCases → Services → Ports
hyperedges.rationale: Demonstrates full hexagonal/ports-and-adapters pattern: inbound port (UseCase interface), application service (implements inbound port, uses outbound ports), infrastructure adapter (implements outbound ports via JPA).

hyperedges.label: Cross-module event integration: Order events consumed by Catalog
hyperedges.rationale: StockEventListener bridges Order and Catalog modules via Spring Modulith ApplicationModuleListener, consuming both OrderItemPaidEvent and OrderItemReleasedEvent to maintain stock consistency.

hyperedges.label: Order Lifecycle Flow: place → finalize → ship
hyperedges.rationale: These three services represent the sequential lifecycle phases of an order aggregate: placing items reserves stock, finalize transitions to PAID/CANCELLED, ship transitions to SHIPPED — all mutating Order domain state.

hyperedges.label: Order Application Guard Exceptions
hyperedges.rationale: All four exceptions are application-layer guard conditions that protect domain invariants: entity existence, ownership, and valid state transitions.

hyperedges.label: OrderController HTTP Request/Response Pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: OrderController acts as the HTTP adapter binding inbound request records to use case commands and mapping domain Order results to OrderResponse — all these nodes form the API boundary layer for the order bounded context.

hyperedges.label: Reservation Expiry Flow
Store Plan Change via Billing Events
JPA Enum-to-String Converter Pattern
Store write flow: load-mutate-save pattern
Hexagonal ports: UseCases (in) + Adapters (out) for Store
Flyway migration chain: V1 -> V2 -> V3 -> V4
Order lifecycle DB tables: orders -> payments & shipments
hyperedges.rationale: payments and shipments both reference orders(id) with UNIQUE FK, modeling one-to-one downstream lifecycle stages of an order

hyperedges.label: Order application service tests all testing core order flow
hyperedges.rationale: These four service tests together cover the complete order item state machine: RESERVED -> PAID -> finalized/cancelled, plus TTL expiry

hyperedges.label: Catalog application service tests covering full product CRUD + stock
hyperedges.rationale: These four service tests together cover the complete product management lifecycle: create, enrich with images and stock, and query

nodes.label: Persistable<UUID> isNew flag pattern for domain-assigned IDs
nodes.rationale: User.create() assigned UUID.randomUUID() so Spring Data JPA saw id != null and called merge() instead of persist(), causing ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException. Fixed by implementing Persistable<UUID> with a @Transient isNew flag set to true in create() and reset to false in @PostLoad, allowing persist() to be called reliably.
nodes.norm_label: persistable<uuid> isnew flag pattern for domain-assigned ids

nodes.label: Spring Security /error path must be in permitAll()
nodes.rationale: When an unhandled exception occurs, Spring forwards internally to /error. If /error is not in permitAll(), AuthorizationFilter blocks it with 403, masking the real error from the client.
nodes.norm_label: spring security /error path must be in permitall()
